note: docs/timings.md can contain a LYING gate row, and I have one to point at. Row 667 on campaign/the-grain: label gate, wall=5.565s user=4.144s sys=1.010s cpu_ratio=0.93 rc=0, on ambrose at 12 cores. A real make gate on that commit took 572.319s in the very next row. gate-run depends on fmt-check clippy type-audit type-audit-report test, and 3348 nextest tests cannot run in 5.5 seconds, so that row records a run whose test phase did not happen -- yet timed.sh appended it with rc=0, which is indistinguishable from a passing gate to anyone reading the ledger later. The 4.1s of user time is about what the cheap half alone costs, so the shape is consistent with the fmt/clippy/type-audit prefix running and the test phase being skipped. Cause not established; I did not debug it. Two consequences for readers: do NOT trust a gate row whose wall time is implausibly small just because rc is 0, and when you cite a gate timing, cite the wall time alongside it so an implausible one is visible. The per-test alarm reads docs/timings/test-baseline-HOST.tsv rather than this file, so the blast radius is human archaeology rather than the alarm.
